speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with episodic cough and shortness of breath; to begin our workup, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since you had symptoms like fever and congestion 8 weeks ago, was there any specific diagnosis or treatment given for that initial illness, and have you noticed any wheezing or chest tightness during these recent episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodic cough and shortness of breath. I also have Cough worsens with exertion and at night, History of recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms such as fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-infectious reactive airway dysfunction (cough-variant asthma).

The history of a recent upper respiratory infection followed by episodic cough, dyspnea on exertion, and nocturnal worsening is classic for this condition. I am requesting a Chest X-Ray to rule out pneumonia or other structural causes before finalizing this diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray
